title: hotfix: fix SLO enforcer race during regional failover causing double load-shedding
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Customers reported increased 429/503 errors during a staged regional failover test; investigation revealed the SLO enforcer could enter a race where two regional controllers concurrently decided to shed the same customer traffic, triggering double load-shedding and unnecessary capacity churn. Reproduction: stress test harness and Canary 42 reproduced the condition when failover concurrency and stale routing cache combined with a delayed lock release. Root cause: the SLO enforcer uses a best-effort distributed lock for per-customer enforcement. During rapid regional failover the lock release and re-acquire path could interleave with a stale routing decision, causing two independent enforcers to both apply aggressive shed policies for the same customer. Fix: 1) make per-customer enforcement idempotent by adding a namespace + generation check to the enforcement key so stale controllers cannot apply policies after a routing generation bump; 2) switch from best-effort lock to a short-lived lease with renewal for enforcer leadership during failover windows; 3) add a fast-path in the enforcer to detect duplicate shedding intents and no-op if the active policy generation is already equal or higher. Also added a small regression test to perf-canary and an e2e that simulates regional failover with concurrent enforcers. Testing: unit tests for lease/renewal, integration test in perf-canary reproducing prior failure no longer fails, manual canary in staging for 48 hours with synthetic traffic, and a limited rollout to region-us-west-2 with metrics observed. Rollout: merged to main and will be backported to 2026.02.x release branch; recommend redeploy of enforcer services with zero-downtime rolling restart and monitor slo_enforcer.shed_duplicates.rate. Checklist: [x] Reproduced locally, [x] Added unit/integration tests, [x] CI green, [x] Staging canary, [x] Backport PR prepared. Related: Linear ENG-2148, ENG-2199. Notes: change is intentionally minimal around runtime hot path and guarded by feature flag 'slo_enforcer_strict_leases' enabled in staging.
